chapter_theme: The first ten ranks one good above another in each line, and repeatedly puts what is kept or practised (conduct, retention, truthfulness, health, shame, chastity, reverence, not dwindling) above what is possessed or displayed (study, brilliance, liberality, youth, beauty, lineage, a large beginning).

1.reading: The opening saying ranks the possession of right conduct above recitation of learning.
1.nuance: Line 1 (ஆர்கலி யுலகத்து மக்கட் கெல்லாம், 'for all people of the sea-roaring world') is the frame repeated at the head of every ten, so the book's first ranking is addressed to everyone, not to one birth or order. ஓதல் is recitation, learning by repeating a text, which is what conduct is set against.

items.claim: having right conduct excels study by recitation

2.reading: Being held in awe by others' eyes is ranked above being loved.
2.nuance: கண்ணஞ்சப் படுதல் is literally 'being feared by the eye': most plainly, being looked on with respectful fear. It could also mean being shrunk from in sight, which would make the saying harsher. The saying names no ruler; the frame addresses everyone, so the awe here is a standing a person holds, not only a king's.

items.claim: being regarded with awe excels being held in affection

3.reading: Not forgetting what one has learnt is ranked above native brilliance.
3.nuance: மேதை is quickness of mind one has without effort; the saying puts a discipline (keeping what was learnt) above a gift.

items.claim: retaining what one has learnt excels sharp native intelligence

4.reading: Truthfulness is ranked above liberality in giving.
4.nuance: வண்மை, open-handedness, is the virtue the bardic poems praise most in a patron; the saying sets a virtue of speech above it.

5.reading: Freedom from bodily disease is ranked above youth.
5.nuance: The saying separates two goods usually counted together: youth without health is not the better thing.

items.claim: being free of bodily disease excels being young

6.reading: A sense of shame is ranked above the possession of beauty or good qualities.
6.nuance: நலனுடைமை can be bodily beauty or excellence in general; either way an outward or possessed good is set below an inner restraint. The saying names no gender.

items.claim: a sense of shame excels having beauty or good qualities

7.reading: The saying ranks chastity above the possession of a good lineage.
7.domain_note: a wife, since கற்பு is the period's word for a woman's marital fidelity
7.nuance: The saying does not name a woman, but கற்பு in this literature is chiefly the wife's virtue, so the ranking reports a norm for women. It also demotes birth: lineage is outranked by conduct, as conduct outranks study in saying 1.

items.claim: chastity excels being of good lineage

norm.note: a norm of the period ranking a woman's chastity above her family's standing

8.reading: Serving and honouring the learned is ranked above learning itself.
8.nuance: வழிபடுதல் is the word for worship and service; the learned are given the reverence due to a deity or teacher.

items.claim: revering and attending on the learned excels one's own learning

9.reading: The saying ranks கற்செய்கை above subduing those who hate one; the ranked thing is most plausibly the practice of learning, against revenge on enemies.
9.nuance: கற்செய்கை is unclear as written: கல் may be learning (கல்-, to learn) or stone, giving 'deeds of firmness'. Either way something built in oneself is set above striking down a foe; the second reading of the word cannot be fixed from the line.

items.claim: the practice the saying calls கற்செய்கை excels crushing one's enemies

10.reading: Not dwindling afterwards is ranked above swelling greatly at the start.
10.nuance: The saying names no subject (wealth, friendship, fortune); it is a rule about any course, valuing what holds over what begins large.

items.claim: not diminishing later excels growing large at first

links.note: Kural 134 says a brahmin can relearn a forgotten Veda but his birth is ruined if conduct fails; saying 1 ranks conduct above recitation for all people.
links.teaches: The Kural's ranking of conduct over recitation, made for the brahmin whose role is recitation, is here lifted off birth entirely and given to everyone the frame line addresses.
links.list_adds: It sets the ranking first in a ten of rankings and removes the brahmin, so conduct over study becomes the opening rule for all people rather than a warning to one varna.

links.note: Both sayings place learning below something else: conduct in 1, serving the learned in 8.
links.teaches: Within one ten learning is twice ranked second, once to conduct and once to reverence for those who have learnt, so the book never lets learning be the highest good.

links.note: Kural 562 tells the ruler to raise the rod sharply but bring it down lightly; saying 2 ranks being held in awe above being loved, on the plainer reading of கண்ணஞ்சப் படுதல்.
links.teaches: The Kural allows awe only as a measured show that must not become harm, while the saying ranks awe over love outright and for anyone, so the pair shows how far the measure matters.
links.list_adds: It ranks awe directly against affection, a contrast the couplet lacks, and carries it beyond the king to every person the frame addresses.

links.note: Kural 300 says nothing seen as true is better than truthfulness; saying 4 sets truthfulness specifically above liberality.
links.teaches: The Kural's absolute claim for truth is tested against the one virtue its rival tradition prizes most, open-handed giving, and truth still wins.
links.list_adds: It names the rival virtue that truth outranks, liberality, where the couplet compares truth with everything at once.

links.note: Naladiyar 55 laments youth gone and disease and old age coming; saying 5 ranks freedom from disease above youth.
links.teaches: The quatrain counts youth's passing and illness's coming as one loss that urges renunciation, while the saying pulls them apart and says health, not youth, is the greater good.
links.list_adds: It ranks two goods the quatrain mourns together, making health a separate and higher thing than youth.

links.note: Kural 1014 calls shame the ornament of the worthy; saying 6 ranks shame above beauty or good qualities.
links.teaches: The Kural's metaphor of shame as an ornament becomes a literal ranking: shame outranks the beauty that ornaments are meant to serve.
links.list_adds: It sets shame against beauty in a direct comparison, turning the couplet's figure into a ranking among goods.

links.note: Kural 54 asks what is greater than a woman with the firmness of chastity; saying 7 names lineage as one of the things chastity outranks.
links.teaches: Where the Kural leaves chastity's superiority open-ended, the saying sets it against birth itself, so a woman's fidelity is made to count for more than the family she comes from.
links.list_adds: It pits chastity against lineage, one specific good of birth, a contrast the couplet does not draw.

links.note: Kural 395 says the foremost are those who learnt while yearning before teachers like the poor before the rich; saying 8 ranks serving the learned above learning.
links.teaches: The Kural makes humility before the learned the posture of learning, while the saying ranks that reverence above the learning it leads to, so the means is put above the end.
links.list_adds: It ranks the service of the learned against learning itself, where the couplet only makes the one the manner of the other.

links.note: Sirupanchamoolam 28 says the fit pupil serves his teacher with love; saying 8 ranks serving the learned above learning.
links.teaches: One counted work names service of the teacher as the mark of a fit pupil and the other ranks it above learning itself, so the group treats reverence for the learned as prior to knowledge.

links.note: Kural 782 says the friendship of the good waxes like the moon and that of fools wanes after being full; saying 10 ranks not dwindling above a large beginning.
links.teaches: The Kural's moon image is about friendship; the saying states its principle bare, for any course of fortune or bond, and keeps only the half that matters: holding, not starting great.
links.list_adds: It strips the image and the domain of friendship and ranks endurance over a large start as a general rule.

source_issues: show flags every saying of this ten (1-10) as site_diff: the online text's verses at these numbers are different sayings, so the edition's numbering or order of the tens differs from the site's.
Line 1 of saying 1 is the frame line repeated at the head of every ten (1, 11, 21 ... 91); it belongs to the ten, not to saying 1 alone.
Saying 10 is spaced முற்பெரு கலின்பின், which divides முற்பெருகலின் பின் at the wrong place.
Saying 9's கற்செய்கை is doubtful as written; the sense of the ranked thing cannot be fixed from the line.
